story_report.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin observed Pacific Fleet naval exercises off Sakhalin Island before visiting Iturup, one of the Russian-controlled Kuril Islands claimed by Japan. Japan called the visit “unacceptable,” with Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi lodging a strong protest and summoning Russia’s ambassador. The trip was Putin’s first visit to the islands, not the first by a Russian leader: former President Dmitry Medvedev visited in 2010. The dispute remains a central obstacle to a formal Japan-Russia peace treaty ending World War II hostilities.

sections.heading: Japan and Russia contest sovereignty
sections.body: Russia controls the Kuril island chain, while Japan claims its four southernmost islands: Iturup, known in Japan as Etorofu; Kunashir; Shikotan; and Habomai. Japan says the Northern Territories are inherently Japanese territory historically and under international law, and its 2025 Diplomatic Bluebook describes them as under Russian occupation. Putin said their current status was established by the outcome of World War II and reflected in international documents.

sections.heading: Putin visit deepens stalled diplomacy
sections.body: During his trip, Putin met Sakhalin regional governor Valery Limarenko and toured a fish plant, hospital and school on Iturup. Japan says Russia discontinued peace-treaty talks in March 2022, suspended related exchange programs and withdrew from discussions on joint economic activity. Tokyo says it will continue seeking a peace treaty through resolution of the islands’ status, but the reviewed material indicates no active negotiating channel has been restored.

event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine War is an ongoing armed conflict between Ukraine and the Russian Federation, rooted in fighting that began in eastern Ukraine in 2014 and greatly escalated with Russia’s full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. It has involved conventional ground operations as well as long-range missile and drone attacks, and has produced a major humanitarian and displacement crisis.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: Conflict-related humanitarian operations in eastern Ukraine expanded in 2014; Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 transformed the conflict into a nationwide emergency.

facts.label: Main parties and geography
facts.value: The war principally involves Ukraine and the Russian Federation, with military operations taking place in Ukraine and attacks increasingly affecting areas beyond the immediate front line.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: On March 2, 2022, the UN General Assembly deplored Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, demanded that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its forces, and reaffirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.

facts.label: International Court of Justice proceedin
facts.value: In provisional measures issued on March 16, 2022 in Ukraine v. Russian Federation, the International Court of Justice ordered Russia to suspend military operations begun on February 24, 2022, while stating that the order did not decide the case’s merits.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The war has driven large-scale displacement, damaged civilian infrastructure and left millions of people in need of assistance; UNHCR describes it as an ongoing full-scale war and humanitarian emergency.

Spain’s next total eclipse visible from the country is scheduled for Aug. 2, 2027; another will not be visible there until 2053.

event_overview.title: About Congo Ebola Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Congo Ebola Outbreak
event_overview.summary: This is the 2026 Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with epidemiologically linked cases reported in neighboring Uganda. The outbreak was declared in May 2026 and has expanded from its initial focus in northeastern DRC amid insecurity, population movement, and constraints on surveillance, isolation, and care.

facts.label: Start and official declaration
facts.value: DRC health authorities declared the country’s 17th recorded Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026, after the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease in samples associated with illness clusters in Ituri Province.

facts.label: Virus involved
facts.value: The event involves Bundibugyo virus disease, rather than the Zaire ebolavirus responsible for DRC’s 2018–2020 outbreak. WHO states that no approved vaccine or specific treatment existed for this virus as the 2026 outbreak began, although candidate countermeasures were being studied.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: Transmission began in Ituri Province, including Mongbwalu, Rwampara and Bunia health zones, and later spread to other DRC provinces. Uganda’s cases were linked to transmission originating in DRC, making this a cross-border regional outbreak rather than an outbreak confined to one locality.

facts.label: International health status
facts.value: On May 17, 2026, the WHO Director-General determined that the epidemic in DRC and Uganda constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern under the International Health Regulations, while stating that it did not meet the separate criteria for a pandemic emergency.

facts.label: Response approach
facts.value: The response is led by the national health authorities with WHO and partner support, emphasizing rapid detection and laboratory confirmation, isolation and clinical care, contact tracing, infection prevention, safe burials, community engagement, and cross-border preparedness.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major reported developments in the 2026 DRC outbreak—such as reported tolls, geographic or regional status, treatment capacity, and workforce issues—rather than providing a complete case ledger, every official situation report, or the full history of Ebola in Central Africa.

Sky News reported that local law-enforcement departments, including U.S. prison settings, have previously used the gloves.

sections.heading: Safety Warnings and Misuse Concerns
sections.body: The manufacturer’s manual warns that any use of force, including the device, may cause or contribute to death or serious injury. It recommends avoiding use on elderly people, small children, pregnant women and severely disabled people, and says the gloves should not be used for verbal defiance, punishment, torture or horseplay; it suggests a maximum 15-second activation for a specified Level 2 event. Former acting ICE director John Sandweg and law professor Michael Mannheimer raised concerns that ready access could encourage misuse or bypass lesser-force options. DHS said ICE reviews equipment decisions for consistency with law-enforcement policies and standards.

sections.body: AP reported that the DHS notice contemplated a no-bid solicitation as early as Friday and a contract lasting through March 31, 2027. The notice therefore indicated a possible purchasing path, rather than confirmation that ICE had acquired or issued the devices.

facts.value: The main earthquake struck on August 10, 2026; rescue and damage-assessment operations continued in the following days.

facts.label: Magnitude and affected area
facts.value: The earthquake was reported as magnitude 7.4 and affected western Colombia, including Pereira, Cali, Quibdó and Manizales; it was also felt in Ecuador and Panama.

facts.label: Pereira’s setting
facts.value: Pereira is the capital of Risaralda department and the largest city in Colombia’s Eje Cafetero (Coffee Axis); it is located in central-western Colombia.

facts.value: The Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC) is the national geological authority that publishes earthquake information and seismic-hazard tools; its seismic catalog contains events from 1993 onward and says entries are manually reviewed by SGC seismology analysts.

facts.label: Response framework
facts.value: Colombia’s disaster-risk system is established under Law 1523 of 2012. The law assigns disaster-risk management to national and territorial authorities and gives the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) a coordinating role across the system.

sections.heading: Remote Chocó Limits Damage Assessment
sections.body: The earthquake’s epicenter was near San José del Palmar in Chocó, where much of the territory can be reached only by boat or plane, according to AP. Phone outages were reported in parts of Quibdó, and authorities initially had limited information on damage and injuries across Chocó. A June disaster-risk alert had also identified San José del Palmar as facing a high forecast landslide risk, a pre-existing hazard that could complicate access but was not identified as earthquake damage.

sections.heading: Emergency Declarations Address Housing Losses
sections.body: President Abelardo de la Espriella declared an emergency to speed earthquake-recovery funding, AP reported. CBS later reported that he declared an economic emergency and three days of national mourning. Official figures cited by CBS put the number of destroyed dwellings above 11,000 and said thousands of families were homeless, while the president said nearly 26,000 families had been affected. The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid and the European Union pledged €2 million.

sections.heading: Pereira Searches Focus on Missing People
sections.body: Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder said rescue efforts were entering their final phase, while the president said the response was focused on people reported missing, CBS reported. In Pereira, local authorities had initially identified at least 15 collapsed buildings where people were feared trapped. At a collapsed bakery, rescuers detected possible signs of life and relatives said a person beneath the rubble appeared to respond to requests to knock, though no successful contact or rescue was independently confirmed. Civilians also joined searches in Cali.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not published a complete, independently verified assessment covering all remote affected areas, leaving the broader damage and casualty picture incomplete.

The number of people still trapped, missing or already located remains unresolved. CBS cited nearly 500 people officially missing, while civilian-run databases listed more than 4,100, figures that cannot be directly compared without knowing how duplicate or resolved reports were handled.
The reviewed reporting does not establish how quickly emergency funding and international aid will reach displaced households, or which localities will be prioritized.

event_overview.title: About Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
event_overview.subject: Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
event_overview.summary: This event concerns lethal violence in the occupied West Bank involving Palestinians, Israeli settlers and, in some incidents, Israeli security forces. It occurs within the broader Israeli-Palestinian conflict, where settlement expansion, access to land, security operations and retaliatory attacks have long made rural communities and roads flashpoints.

facts.label: Location and status
facts.value: The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is part of the Palestinian territory occupied by Israel since 1967 in the terminology used by the United Nations and the International Court of Justice.

facts.label: Governance framework
facts.value: The 1995 Israeli-Palestinian Interim Agreement (Oslo II) set interim arrangements for Palestinian self-government, security, elections and administration in the West Bank and Gaza pending a permanent-status settlement; it was designed as a five-year interim framework, not a final peace agreement.

facts.label: Settlement legal context
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2334 states that Israeli settlements in Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, have no legal validity and are a violation of international law. In its July 19, 2024 advisory opinion, the ICJ found that Israel’s transfer and maintenance of settlers in the West Bank and East Jerusalem is contrary to Article 49(6) of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

facts.label: Violence pattern
facts.value: UN OCHA defines settler-related violence broadly as violence, intimidation or trespass carried out by or against Israeli settlers and other Israeli civilians in the West Bank. Its incident classification distinguishes attacks by the identity of the initiator and can include alleged settler perpetrators, Israeli forces intervening in such incidents, Palestinian civilians and other actors.

facts.label: Protection and accountability context
facts.value: The ICJ’s 2024 advisory opinion found that settler violence against Palestinians, ineffective prevention or punishment of it, and excessive force can contribute to a coercive environment; this is a legal finding of the Court concerning Israel’s international obligations, rather than a determination of responsibility for any one incident.

event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine War is an ongoing armed conflict between Ukraine and the Russian Federation, rooted in fighting that began in eastern Ukraine in 2014 and greatly escalated with Russia’s full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. It has involved conventional ground operations as well as long-range missile and drone attacks, and has produced a major humanitarian and displacement crisis.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: Conflict-related humanitarian operations in eastern Ukraine expanded in 2014; Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 transformed the conflict into a nationwide emergency.

facts.label: Main parties and geography
facts.value: The war principally involves Ukraine and the Russian Federation, with military operations taking place in Ukraine and attacks increasingly affecting areas beyond the immediate front line.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: On March 2, 2022, the UN General Assembly deplored Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, demanded that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its forces, and reaffirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.

facts.label: International Court of Justice proceedin
facts.value: In provisional measures issued on March 16, 2022 in Ukraine v. Russian Federation, the International Court of Justice ordered Russia to suspend military operations begun on February 24, 2022, while stating that the order did not decide the case’s merits.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The war has driven large-scale displacement, damaged civilian infrastructure and left millions of people in need of assistance; UNHCR describes it as an ongoing full-scale war and humanitarian emergency.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on specified late-July and early-August 2026 security developments, including cross-border drone or missile incidents and strikes; it does not aim to provide a complete account of the war’s military, diplomatic, legal, or humanitarian history.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict involving the United States, Iran and Israel, centered on attacks, counterattacks and threats affecting Iran, neighboring states and maritime traffic in and around the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials said combat operations began on February 28, 2026, citing self-defense, protection of regional forces and allies, and freedom of maritime commerce; the United Nations has called for de-escalation, protection of civilians and compliance with international law.

facts.label: Start and parties
facts.value: The conflict’s current phase began on February 28, 2026. The United States notified the UN that it had commenced combat operations against Iran in cooperation with Israel; the UN Secretary-General also described subsequent Iranian attacks affecting Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz—between Iran and Oman, linking the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea—is a central theater because its security directly affects regional shipping and energy exports.

facts.label: Maritime and energy stakes
facts.value: Disruption to shipping through Hormuz has been a major international consequence: EIA reported that military action and the resulting de facto closure sharply reduced oil flows and contributed to large price increases in early 2026.

facts.label: Diplomatic and legal framework
facts.value: The UN has urged an immediate cessation of hostilities and stated that all parties must uphold the UN Charter, protect civilians under international humanitarian law and preserve nuclear safety. In the United States, the War Powers Resolution requires presidential consultation with Congress where possible and a written report within 48 hours when U.S. forces are introduced into hostilities without a declaration of wa

facts.label: Broader policy context
facts.value: The conflict occurs alongside longstanding international concern over Iran’s nuclear programme. UN Security Council Resolution 2231, adopted in 2015 to endorse the JCPOA, remains part of that background; the UN says earlier Iran-related Security Council measures were re-applied on September 27, 2025.

event_overview.title: About Colombia Earthquake
event_overview.subject: Colombia Earthquake
event_overview.summary: The Colombia earthquake was a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck western Colombia on August 10, 2026, causing major building damage and trapping people beneath collapsed structures. Pereira, in the coffee-growing region of Risaralda, was among the affected cities, and the event prompted a continuing search-and-rescue and disaster-response operation.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The main earthquake struck on August 10, 2026; rescue and damage-assessment operations continued in the following days.

facts.label: Magnitude and affected area
facts.value: The earthquake was reported as magnitude 7.4 and affected western Colombia, including Pereira, Cali, Quibdó and Manizales; it was also felt in Ecuador and Panama.

facts.label: Pereira’s setting
facts.value: Pereira is the capital of Risaralda department and the largest city in Colombia’s Eje Cafetero (Coffee Axis); it is located in central-western Colombia.

facts.label: Seismic monitoring
facts.value: The Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC) is the national geological authority that publishes earthquake information and seismic-hazard tools; its seismic catalog contains events from 1993 onward and says entries are manually reviewed by SGC seismology analysts.

facts.label: Response framework
facts.value: Colombia’s disaster-risk system is established under Law 1523 of 2012. The law assigns disaster-risk management to national and territorial authorities and gives the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) a coordinating role across the system.

items.title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Could Become Deadliest in History, WHO Warns
items.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Congo, declared on May 15, has already resulted in over 2,000 deaths and thousands of additional reported cases. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus indicated that if the current trend continues, this outbreak could surpass the deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded during the West African epidemic from 2014 to 2016. items.title: ICE to Spend $20 Million on Electric Shock Gloves for Officers
items.text: The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) plans to invest up to $20 million in gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks. These gloves are intended to compel compliance from individuals during encounters with officers.

items.title: Drone Strike on Passenger Train in Odesa Region Results in Fatalities
items.text: On August 13, 2026, a Russian Shahed drone struck a passenger train in the Berezivka district of Ukraine's Odesa region. The attack resulted in the deaths of the train driver and his assistant, while 340 passengers, including 67 children, were evacuated from the train.
